video_title: Jalen Duren & KAT's BIG Contract Questions & Houston's Expectations | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' contract extension status and its impact on the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Karl-Anthony Towns and his on-again, off-again contract extensions with the Knicks

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: We are going to talk about Karl-Anthony Towns and his on-again, off-again contract extensions with the Knicks and what kind of factor that could be going into this season.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I think it's a huge factor. It's a distraction. You want your stars focused on winning, not on contract negotiations. It's a business, but it can definitely affect chemistry.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's contract impasse with the Detroit Pistons
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons and Duren have been at an impasse over contract talks.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I want to start with Jalen Duren, who as we record this on Friday morning, September 25th, does not have a new contract with the Detroit Pistons. The Pistons and Duren have been at an impasse over contract talks. The Pistons are reportedly offering five years, $200 million. Duren believes he is worth more, coming off an all-NBA season. There is the possibility he could take the qualifying offer, which is at about $10 million, and become an unrestricted free agent next offseason.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I think the Pistons are handling it the correct way. They are rewarding him for a high level of play, but they are trying to think for the future. They are going to give him $40 million a year to play basketball. They are trying to build a great team around him, but most importantly, a top-10 player like Cade Cunningham.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's performance decline in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: His numbers were basically cut in half. He was outplayed by other bigs.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The facts are that if Jalen Duren had pulled his hamstring on the final day of the regular season, we wouldn't be having this conversation because the Pistons would have maxed him out. What is giving the Pistons reason for pause is what happened in the playoffs, which were a disaster for Jalen Duren. His numbers were basically cut in half. He was outplayed by other bigs, and he just didn't look like the franchise center that he looked like for most of the regular season.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: He was physically dominated. Wendell Carter was not worried about him at all. They were happy to see him. It was like, hey, we can win if he is going to play. That is what makes me seem like the $50 million is getting taken away, because it is like, bro, you are supposed to anchor that front line, that paint. Nobody is scared of you, muscle man.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons' difficult position regarding Jalen Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: They can't just lose him for nothing. They can't. It's already been a weird offseason in Detroit.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The Pistons are between a rock and a hard place here because they can't just lose him for nothing. They can't. It's already been a weird offseason in Detroit. They trade away Isaiah Stewart to see what you want about his anger issues out there on the floor, but he was a part of the fabric of that new old-school Detroit basketball. They lose Tobias Harris, a productive guy for the two years. The Pistons in the last two years have engineered one of the great revivals in the NBA. No coincidence Tobias Harris was on the Pistons for those two years. You replace him with John Collins, who is younger, I guess, but John Collins has been moved around a lot.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: Analytics helps John Collins' game a lot because when you sit there, you watch it, it helps nobody but him. I love John Collins to death, but his game helps nobody but him.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The risks of Jalen Duren signing a qualifying offer
quotes.excerpt: You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The qualifying offer is different because in a lot of contracts, let's use Jalen Brunson as an example. Jalen Brunson took less money from the Knicks. Well, Jalen Brunson can make that up. Jalen Brunson can get all that money back when he signs the next contract. You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back. You're never going to be able to recoup the difference between the one-year $10 million qualifying offer that you signed and the $50 million average salary that you would sign if you're Jalen Duren there. So it's a lot of money, and it's a big bet on yourself.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I also think, man, if you give him $250 million and you're trapped with him having those playoff performances and being a regular season superhero, it's going to be held to tell the captain regardless.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' contract situation and the Knicks' financial constraints
quotes.excerpt: Towns is eligible for a four-year, $275 million extension. This money is just wild in today's NBA.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Karl-Anthony Towns is eligible for a four-year, $275 million extension. This money is just wild in today's NBA. Towns is not going to get that, but it does seem like the Knicks want him to take something of a discount so they can continue to build the team around Towns, around Brunson, around OG Anunoby, around Bridges, and around the championship core that they have. You've got an owner in James Dolan who says we're not going into the second apron. Something here has to give.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: After winning a championship for the first time in 50-plus years, I feel like that should be rewarded on top of the fact of being like, hey, we're trying to build a team around you.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Expectations for the Houston Rockets this season
quotes.excerpt: Ime Udoka says that he wants this team in Houston to make some real noise this season.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Ime Udoka says that he wants this team in Houston to make some real noise this season. The Rockets, of course, have Fred VanVleet back. You've got Reed Sheppard having himself look like a good offseason. What do you think is the ceiling for the Houston Rockets? Do you think this Rockets team, with the changes they made the offseason, how healthy they get going into this season, is this a team that can compete for a championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I like the fact they added little pieces that can provide fight when things are dwindling. So Marcus Smart, even though he has his moments, he does have championship toughness and he plays with a certain energy that's going to get you over top.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of losing Dillon Brooks on the Rockets' defense
quotes.excerpt: When they lost Dillon Brooks, that was like a piece that could have got them over the top.
quotes.quote: I feel like when they lost Dillon Brooks, that was like a piece that could have got them over the top in the sense of playoffs or made certain games more serious. I feel like with the top teams, it's not in regards to talent, but they lose in regards to heart. You know what I mean? Or when you start seeing certain parts in a season, even last year, we're like, oh, we foresaw this coming probably like a month before ever happened, them getting eliminated by a lower Lakers team, you know? So I think with Ime Udoka, he's probably just like, man, the healthier the merrier, but let me get some dogs, so I can have depth and keep rotating in and out so we don't go through, shout out to Tari Eason, we don't go through two months of his headache of trying to make a shot.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Fred VanVleet's performance and impact on the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Is Fred VanVleet the same player or better than he was before the injury?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Is Fred VanVleet the same player or better than he was before the injury? They missed Fred VanVleet last year, man. They missed him a lot more than I thought they were going to miss him because I thought that Aman Thompson would be perfectly adequate as a playmaker. And look, he was fine. He just doesn't have the requisite experience to slow the game down and to understand what to do in big moments. Fred VanVleet's won a championship. Fred VanVleet has made some huge shots for a championship team. Getting him back and bumping everybody down a role, that's going to be big.

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I think one thing I'm excited about him coming back is just leadership. Last year, I felt like Aman Thompson would have been able to adapt more in playmaker role if there was more vocal leaders around. I think there was a couple of vets around and a lot of young guys still trying to find their footing underneath them.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Fred VanVleet's role and value as a championship-level point guard
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if Fred VanVleet is a championship guard. And that's a point guard.
quotes.quote: I don't know if Fred VanVleet is a championship guard. And that's a point guard. But he does have a situation where I think if Ime Udoka comes out, Reed Shepard could be a six-man or vice versa, but they can kind of share the starting role, lead guard role, six-man role depending on how the game is going to go. I feel like I love Fred VanVleet, I love what he stands for. I just never thought he was a first-guard. I think that championship run always was unbelievable. I thought how he shot, how his toughness, even at Wichita State and everything else. But when it comes to the best position in the league, you got to make sure that that gun is is elite as opposed to you just shooting like he shoots like a Hall of Famer. He's kind of like the modern day Mike Bibby, if you think about it.
